name: Registered Dietitian Nutritionist
description: Dietitians assess nutritional status and design the medical nutrition therapy that treats kidney disease, diabetes, cancer, critical illness and failure to thrive. ⚠ A median of $76,400 with 8% growth. ⚠⚠⚠ And the thing a Florida student must not get wrong: since 1 January 2024 the national credential requires a GRADUATE DEGREE, while the Florida licensing statute still says a bachelor's — three sources disagree about what this career needs, and this page sets out which one binds.
credentialNote: ⚠⚠⚠ Three standards apply here and they do not agree. ONE, the NATIONAL CREDENTIAL: since 1 January 2024 the Commission on Dietetic Registration has required a minimum of a GRADUATE DEGREE to establish eligibility for the registration examination for dietitians. Anyone who established eligibility on or before 31 December 2023, or who is already registered, is not affected. The graduate degree may be in ANY field from an accredited institution, but the ACEND-accredited coursework and a supervised practice component of at least 1,000 hours — most programmes run about 1,200 — remain separate requirements. TWO, the FLORIDA LICENCE: s. 468.509 still requires only a baccalaureate or postbaccalaureate degree with a major in human nutrition, food and nutrition, dietetics or food management, plus a preprofessional experience component of not less than 900 hours, plus a state examination — from which registered dietitians are exempt. THREE, the BLS still lists typical entry-level education as a bachelor's degree. ⚠⚠ Reconcile them this way: the Florida licence is what makes practice lawful, the RDN is what makes you employable, and the RDN now needs the master's. ⚠ O*NET's respondents already reflect the new reality — 53% name a post-baccalaureate certificate and 33% a master's, against only 10% naming a bachelor's.
bodyHtml:
What the work actually is

O*NET, on dietitians and nutritionists: assess nutritional needs, diet restrictions, and current health plans to develop and implement dietary-care plans; counsel individuals and groups on basic rules of good nutrition, healthy eating habits, and nutrition monitoring; manage quantity food service departments or clinical and community nutrition services; plan, conduct, and evaluate dietary, nutritional, and epidemiological research.

⚠ The clinical half is not about healthy eating. Medical nutrition therapy for a dialysis patient, a burns patient or someone on parenteral feeding is prescription-level work with narrow tolerances, and it is why the credential exists. The third task on that list — running food service for a hospital or a school district — is a management job that a large share of dietitians actually do.

The numbers, and they are good

  • O*NET (2024–34): 90,900 employed, growth faster than average (5% to 6%), 6,200 openings a year, median $76,400 (2025).
  • BLS OOH (2025–35): 86,300 jobs, growth 8%, much faster than average, +6,700.

✅ Both are positive and the BLS is the more optimistic — 8% against O*NET's 5–6% band, on different decades. A $76,400 median is solid for a health profession outside the licensed-therapy group, and the work is largely weekday and outpatient or hospital-based.

⚠⚠⚠ The 2024 credential change, and why three sources disagree

This is the most consequential thing on the page and it is recent enough that much of the advice online predates it.

SourceWhat it says you needStatus
Commission on Dietetic Registration⚠ a GRADUATE DEGREE, plus ACEND coursework and 1,000+ supervised hours✅ in force since 1 January 2024
Florida statute s. 468.509a baccalaureate or postbaccalaureate degree, 900 hours, state examinationcurrent state law
BLS Occupational Outlook Handbooktypical entry-level education: bachelor's degree⚠ lagging the change

⚠⚠ They are all accurate about different things, and the practical answer is the strictest one. Florida's licence is what makes practice lawful; the RDN is what employers hire, what the statute itself treats as exempting you from the state examination, and what now requires a master's. Plan for the graduate degree.

⚠ One piece of genuinely good news inside the rule: the graduate degree does not have to be in nutrition. Any accredited master's or doctorate satisfies it — business, public health, psychology, exercise science. What cannot be substituted is the ACEND-accredited coursework and the supervised practice hours, which are assessed separately. So a student who already holds an unrelated master's is closer to this career than they think.

⚠⚠ Florida's funnel is three institutions wide

Only four Florida public institutions award the dietetics bachelor's — FIU 76, UNF 52, UF 33 — and only three award the master's the credential now requires: FIU 41, UNF 28, FSU 12. About 81 graduate credentials a year for the entire state.

⚠⚠⚠ Set that against the 167 bachelor's degrees a year and the shape of the problem is obvious: the 2024 change turned a reasonably open undergraduate pipeline into a narrow graduate bottleneck at three universities. Geography will constrain this decision more than your grades will, and the supervised practice placement — the dietetic internship — has historically been the competitive step even before the master's requirement.

⚠ So ask every programme two questions in writing: is your graduate programme ACEND-accredited, and is the supervised practice built in or do I apply for it separately? A coordinated programme that includes the internship removes the single biggest point of failure in this career.

⚠ The dietetic technician is a different job, not a smaller version

Florida also awards a dietetic technician certificate — Lindsey Hopkins Technical College, about 24 a year. It is a real job (DTR) working under a dietitian's supervision, and it is not a step toward the RDN. The registration route runs through the ACEND didactic programme and a graduate degree; technician hours do not substitute for either.

⚠ It is still worth knowing about as a way into a clinical nutrition department while studying, in the same way phlebotomy works for laboratory science.

✅ What travels, and the prefix that does not

The prerequisites travel well: CHM 2210 Organic Chemistry I at 29 institutions, BSC 2085 and BSC 2086 Anatomy and Physiology at 20 and 19, MCB 2010 Microbiology at 16, STA 2023 and PSY 2012 at 39 and 33. HUN 1201 Nutrition reaches 21 institutions and HUN 2201 Science of Human Nutrition 13.

⚠⚠ The professional prefix does not travel at all, because it barely exists. DIE 3213 Nutrition Therapy is carried by ONE institution and DIE 4125 by two. That is not fragmentation in the usual sense — it is simply how few places teach this. Take the sciences at a state college with confidence and expect the professional sequence to happen in one place.

⚠ Watch which nutrition course you take. HUN 1201 is the general-education nutrition course that health programmes across this site require; HUN 2201 Science of Human Nutrition is the majors version, carried by the universities. They are not interchangeable for a dietetics degree requirement.

Necessary skills

  • Biochemistry, properly. Metabolism is the subject; organic chemistry and biochemistry are where it is learned, and they are the courses that filter this major.
  • Clinical assessment and calculation. Energy and protein requirements, fluid balance, feeding rates — arithmetic with consequences.
  • Counselling without lecturing. Most of the health gain depends on what a patient does at home, and telling them is not the same as changing it.
  • Reading the evidence. Nutrition is the field most saturated with confident nonsense, and the professional's value is knowing what is actually established.
  • Management. Food service is a large employer of dietitians and it is budgets, staff and logistics.

Advice

⚠⚠ Plan for the master's from the first year. The 2024 rule is not being phased in — it is in force, and a bachelor's alone no longer reaches the examination. Anyone advising you otherwise is working from pre-2024 information, including some of the federal material.

⚠ Target a coordinated programme if you can. The supervised practice placement is the historic bottleneck in this profession; a programme that includes it removes that risk entirely.

⚠ If you already hold a master's in something else, look again. The graduate requirement is field-agnostic. You may need only the ACEND coursework and the supervised practice, which is a far shorter route than starting over.

And take the chemistry seriously and early. Organic chemistry is the course that ends dietetics ambitions, it is carried at 29 Florida institutions so you can take it anywhere, and doing it well is the cheapest way to keep this career available.

cipCodes.note: ⚠ Public health — a genuine adjacent destination for the community and population half of nutrition, and one that does not carry the RDN's graduate-degree and internship gate. 15 Florida public institutions against 6 here.

Kinesiology and exercise science — 16 Florida public institutions. Sports nutrition sits across the two, and an exercise science degree plus the ACEND coursework is one of the field-agnostic graduate routes the 2024 rule allows.

Biological sciences — 15 Florida public institutions and the largest science footprint in the state. Named because the metabolism and biochemistry that dietetics rests on are taught here, and because a biology degree plus ACEND coursework is a viable route.

programs.note: The programme itself — and read its degrees note before choosing an institution, because the 2024 graduate-degree rule narrowed Florida's route to three universities awarding about 81 master's credentials a year.

⚠ Not a route here, but the comparison most health-science students are actually making, and it is stark on access: 78 Florida institutions against 6, and licensure from an associate degree against a required master's. ⚠⚠ Named so the reader sees the trade honestly — dietetics is a longer, narrower and more academic route to a similar hospital.

⚠ Not a route. Named because it is the other small, science-heavy clinical programme with a narrow Florida footprint and a long credential chain — and because it reaches its credential from a bachelor's, which is now the practical difference between them.

courses.reason: Science of Human Nutrition — 13 institutions. ⚠ The MAJORS nutrition course, carried by the universities, and the one a dietetics degree requires.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ Not interchangeable with HUN1201 Nutrition (21 institutions), which is the general-education course other health programmes on this site require. Taking the wrong one is a common and avoidable delay.

courses.reason: Nutrition — 21 institutions. The general-education course, widely carried and useful — but check before assuming it satisfies a dietetics requirement.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Listed so the distinction from HUN2201 is visible from both sides.

courses.reason: Organic Chemistry I — 29 institutions. ⚠⚠ The course that filters this major. Metabolism is organic chemistry applied to people, and biochemistry assumes it.
courses.variantNote: ✅ Carried at 29 Florida public institutions, so it can be taken almost anywhere. ⚠ Usually paired with CHM2210L (26 institutions), and preceded by general chemistry CHM2045/2046.

courses.reason: Anatomy and Physiology I — 20 institutions. The structural and functional basis for clinical assessment.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Two equivalent packagings: BSC2085 plus BSC2085L at 20 institutions, the combined BSC2085C at 7.

courses.reason: Anatomy and Physiology II — 19 institutions. Digestive, renal and endocrine systems, which is most of what medical nutrition therapy acts on.
Microbiology — 16 institutions. Foodborne illness and food safety, and the infection context of clinical nutrition.
Food Safety and Sanitation — 8 institutions. HACCP and food service safety, aimed at the management half of the profession that students routinely underestimate.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Often the course that carries a ServSafe or equivalent certification, which is directly employable.

courses.reason: Life Span Nutrition — 5 institutions. Requirements from pregnancy through infancy, childhood, adulthood and old age, which is the framework most clinical practice is organised around.
Nutrition Therapy — ⚠ ONE institution. Medical nutrition therapy proper: the disease-by-disease clinical content the credential exists for.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ Carried by a single Florida public institution, which is not fragmentation but scarcity — only four award this degree at all. ⚠ Expect the professional sequence to happen entirely at one institution, and plan the transfer around the sciences instead.

courses.reason: Management of Food and Nutrition Services — 2 institutions. Budgets, staffing and operations for hospital and institutional food service, which employs a large share of dietitians.
Elementary Statistics — 39 institutions. Nutrition is a field saturated with weak evidence, and the professional's value is being able to tell which studies mean anything.
Introduction to Psychology — 33 institutions. Behaviour change is the mechanism by which nutrition advice works or fails, and counselling is half the job.
English Composition I — 39 institutions. Chart notes, care plans and patient education materials are the written output, and the patient education has to be readable by the patient.
